item.title: Video Editing with Da Vinci Resolve Parts I and II — Tue Nov 10, 6:30 PM — Davenport
item.description: This two part introductory series will cover the layout, tools and workflow used for video editing in DaVinci Resolve. Part I, which will take place on November 10th , will cover basic video editing techniques such as inserting and trimming media, transitions, titles, adding audio, and using flags and markers. Part II will be held on November 17th , where participants will become familiar with some of the more advanced tools in DaVinci’s Editing page such as key framing transform effects, cropping, adjusting clip speed, normalizing audio, and simple compositing. Computers will be provided for this program. item.title: 3D Design with Onshape — Wed Nov 11, 12:30 PM — Flemingdon Park
item.description: Learn how to create parametric designs using cloud based software Onshape. This hands-on workshop introduces participants to the fundamentals of 3D design using Onshape, a cloud-based CAD software. Whether you're an aspiring engineer, designer, or hobbyist, this session provides the tools and knowledge to start creating your own 3D models. What You’ll Learn: Getting Started: Overview of Onshape's interface, navigation tools, and cloud-based collaboration features. Core Design Principles: Understanding 3D modeling basics, including sketches, extrusions, and revolutions. Hands-On Practice: Creating simple 3D parts, assembling components, and exploring design modifications. Best Practices: Tips for efficient modeling, managing design iterations, and exporting models for 3D printing or other applications. This program is ideal for beginners with no prior experience in CAD software, as well as those looking to explore Onshape's capabilities. Registration will start 2 weeks before this class

item.title: The Writings of David Thompson on His Travels in North America — Wed Nov 11, 5:30 PM — North York Central Library
item.description: The Writings of David Thompson This presentation examines the historical Writings of David Thompson. Between 1784 and 1812, David Thompson (1770-1857) explored and traded over a vast expanse of western North America. Later in life, the surveyor and fur trader wrote what he called his Travels , a spectacular geographical and spirited intellectual journey of the Canadian experience. His story tells of a remarkable life in the fur trade but it also captures hid reflections on the land and the indigenous peoples of western North America. Presented by Bill Moreau, editor of the three-volume work, The Writings of David Thompson . Registration is encouraged but not necessary. item.description: There is more information about your world than you might think, and the tools to make sense of it are more accessible than ever. This session introduces public data sources like the Toronto Open Data Portal and Kaggle, then shows you how AI tools can help you explore and analyze that data without any technical background. You will learn how to find datasets relevant to a civic issue, ask AI the right questions to surface insights, and turn raw numbers into something meaningful. No experience required. Arrive 30 minutes before or stay 30 minutes after the program for one-on-one consultations. This program is part of TPL's Innovator in Residence series focused on civic innovation. From October 5 to November 28, join programs, workshops and one-on-one consultations led by technology strategist Ismail Mohamud to learn how technology can help you create positive change in your community. item.title: Coding with Python II — Fri Nov 13, 12:30 PM — Flemingdon Park
item.description: Python is an open source programming language that is used for creating web applications, web content, mathematics and system scripting. In this second Python session we will leverage everything we learned about loops and blocks in part one to create our very own functions. We'll take a look at how to approach function design, how to allow users to enter data into functions through arguments, and how to get our functions to return results. We will also introduce some new data structures which, unlike variables, can hold more than one piece of data at a time. This class is for beginners but assumes you have a basic understanding of Python or have attended Coding with Python I. Registration will start 2 weeks before this class. Computers will be provided.
